```{r setup}
library(lavaan.pl)
```

Ordinal data for a factor model with many items can be simulated with `lavaan::simulateData()`, writing the population model with `paste()`.

```{r}
# p = number of items, q = number of latent variables, n = number of observations
p <- 30; q <- 5; n <- 1000
items <- paste0("y", 1:p)
factors <- paste0("F", 1:q)
factor_of <- rep(seq_len(q), each = p / q)

# Random loadings and latent correlations, the same thresholds for every item
set.seed(123)
loadings <- runif(p, .4, .8)
R <- cov2cor(crossprod(matrix(rnorm(q * q), q)) + diag(q))
thr <- c(-1.5, 0, 1.5)

pairs <- which(upper.tri(R), arr.ind = TRUE)
population <- c(
  paste(factors, "=~", tapply(paste0(loadings, "*", items), factor_of, paste, collapse = " + ")),
  paste0(factors[pairs[, 1]], " ~~ ", R[pairs], "*", factors[pairs[, 2]]),
  paste0(factors, " ~~ 1*", factors),
  paste0(items, " | ", paste0(thr, "*t", seq_along(thr), collapse = " + "))
)
dat <- lavaan::simulateData(population, sample.nobs = n, seed = 123)
head(dat[, 1:6])
```

The model to fit has the same structure, with free parameters.

```{r}
model <- paste(factors, "=~", tapply(items, factor_of, paste, collapse = " + "))
fit <- pmlcfa(model, dat, std.lv = TRUE, ordered = TRUE)
pe <- parameterEstimates(fit)
head(data.frame(pe[pe$op == "=~", c("lhs", "op", "rhs", "est", "se")], true = loadings))
```
